notes.title: Summer Development Update from Drinkbox Studios
notes.content: [p]Hey! How’s it going?  [/p][p]Eating well? Sleeping in? Folding clothes? [/p][p]That’s so great to hear.[/p][p][/p][p]- Oh, us? Nah, we haven’t been up to much. [/p][p]Well, except for all the work we’ve put into our new game [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2974160/Blighted/"][u]Blighted[/u][/url]. Check it out![/p][p][/p][p]As you know, we [url="https://steamcommunity.com/games/2974160/announcements/detail/533226373233248985"][u]announced[/u][/url] Blighted back in June as part of [url="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9JHPGemT0gI&ab_channel=thegameawards"][u]Summer Game Fest 2025[/u][/url], and we’ve been hard at work on it since. (Thanks for wishlisting it, by the way. It really does help 🙏)[/p][p][/p][p]We don’t want to spoil too much, buuuut we’ve added a TON of enemies to the game, and are still adding more! Each of them deadly in their own weird and freaky little way.[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcGirw8Xgso8NdeflBw5tE3v9twKbLroA8soxm1P_mNAdGmdkZ5C9_bJyPOj2GZDyuTPcmwgHdYx6G8IqpUKWSmOjzHdpvdjUPkOhc04Oza7_x-x0lJfhnmYhKJKRH3fZxsfhy88A?key=ufPMY9caO1Pf00_ctoTGWQ"][/img][/p][p]It’s hard to believe but we actually built out an early version of the entire game as part of an internal-alpha milestone! And right now we’re in the middle of tearing it all up, choosing the best bits, adding juicy challenges and putting it all back together again.[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcB7WNc_ID7rJSXKc1JFCllZP1WG7931zeX0LzGzcbE39r41XNQEUhoFPC5fPW3r2ME0EwTgIr5yNacpA3YQVbiCgsbbN0d3VURjWpuC0UxvbzdqJl4Kz1GFr88HvST0So6Vln-3Q?key=ufPMY9caO1Pf00_ctoTGWQ"][/img][/p][p]Now, it might sound like we don’t have much left to do, but that couldn’t be further from the truth! We’re still fine tuning the gameplay and combat loop to go beyond the standard we’ve established in any of our other games thus far. Blight is getting deadlier, and gnarlier too. Our programmers are working all sorts of technical magic to make Blighted shine, ooze and wriggle. And every new object in the game is another opportunity for our artists to draw up a fresh nightmarish creation to populate the growing world. And Jim Guthrie is still sending us tracks that put shivers down our spines in all of the best ways.[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdS_wktGXW5cZQpDDjZt3wW6YyMfT8JOuDx3nTPCVZ09bmpu-1zeVOE7mKbCfz3RxLrI_0weblRZDYIhxJnt5lL6L0ZvElUxzM4LaMA6zo8hz-WDj0LxC1uAYI-FOXRAFfLqGL8vg?key=ufPMY9caO1Pf00_ctoTGWQ"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]We're also prepping the soundtrack from Tales from Space: Mutant Blobs Attack to be released on Steam very soon! As one of our first major releases, Mutant Blobs Attack will always hold a special place in our ears - because the soundtrack by Peter Chapman and Shaun Hatton is SO GOOD. If you ever need a shot of caffeine directly into your earlobes, load up this soundtrack, sit back, and get back up again because your toes will not stop tapping.[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcLSBqlew1oYLAN1HV9oezPGECMjlVP1r4NB60tS529tzdSypMl_0bJVfLRJZz_hjtCOLy1nLpgeY7kSNurU6ldRLcLNQ3oz2_pudPhbuFnB3ZoxyzqBpNN0xonYoR_d-smP7VDZQ?key=ufPMY9caO1Pf00_ctoTGWQ"][/img][/p][p]On the more human side, we recently took the team out to get their quarterly quota of exercise by running, jumping, dodging, ducking, dipping, diving, dodging, throwing, shooting (basketball), shooting (gun) and yelling with [url="http://playactivate.com"][u]Activate[/u][/url]. We then gathered for our biggest team photo to date!! (we’re still missing an international co-worker or two, but we’ll get them one day!)[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeGWP9bjPXc4TEF92lcb1cSn1rR7NMcd0_by5CbjprrIM9GQYpW25AntKL0Bb19xy4CZGFkhEORf8QcQ8pXc_6JxiaBuTCzExVvUUCiAWpYA4fbJlkbls86-kz4bFPP_1RkQSmY?key=ufPMY9caO1Pf00_ctoTGWQ"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Huh. Turns out we have in fact been ‘up to much’! Sorry for all the yapping. As a thank you for listening, we’ve put [url="https://store.steampowered.com/developer/drinkbox/list/48544"][u]all of our games[/u][/url] on sale on Steam![/p][p][/p][p]Catch you later![/p][p]The Drinkbox Team[/p]

notes.title: Announcing our new game Blighted
notes.content: [p]Hello hello! We have some very exciting news to share!  We'd like to introduce you to [url="https://www.drinkboxstudios.com/games/blighted"]Blighted[/url], a Metroidvania Action-RPG set in a psychedelic western nightmare world, and our most ambitious project to date! [/p][p] Blighted features some of the most intense combat Drinkbox has ever put together, and for the first time in 3D! Time your attacks, read your enemies and capitalize on powerful finishers to survive deadly encounters. Punches will not be pulled!  [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/6863330/b91051b436a2ff35fc887775bb49c7a3be72dd21.gif"][/img][/p][p]We're also excited to debut what we're calling the [i]Blight[/i] system. Tracking skillful plays, the Blight system responds by ratcheting up the difficulty. At higher levels of Blight, enemy behaviors, player abilities and the surrounding environment can all change.  [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/6863330/c9561984667d1dc1ee4c410e45aebed3b78d80b5.gif"][/img][/p][p]Consume the brains of defeated bosses to reclaim lost memories and learn ethereal abilities. Use your newfound powers to complete special challenges and uncover hidden paths.  [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/6863330/466cccfd877be46c7ecf340e8b183e17805cd71a.gif"][/img][/p][p]Featuring music by the acclaimed composer [url="https://jimguthrie.bandcamp.com/"]Jim Guthrie[/url] (who also worked with us on [i]Nobody Saves the World[/i]), jam along to hauntingly beautiful tracks as you play solo, or in co-op!  [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/6863330/0e3a67165c01a154425f158063acb3c727eeebad.gif"][/img][/p][p]Wishlist the game to get notified when the game launches. Wishlisting also helps boost our Steam launch visibility, so is doubly appreciated.  [/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2974160/Blighted/"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]Finally, please consider [url="https://discord.gg/XXXtbjvx7j"]joining our Discord[/url] to keep up with news and updates about Blighted. Or to just hop in to say hi :)  Thank you all for your support. We can't wait to reveal more about the game soon!  All the best, The Drinkbox Team  [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/6863330/2cbac35e7efd9c884b9fee3beb6b4858b2510b2f.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Nobody's Seen This Concept Art!
notes.content:
Hey everyone! We recently took a little stroll down memory lane and gathered a bunch of concept art for Nobody Saves the World, a lot of which has never been seen before! (even by some of us!)

Nobody Saves the World might already seem full of lots of different ideas, but for every 1 idea that made it into the game, there were 10 that we had to whittle down from!

Starting with a whole bunch of forms we thought about adding! From assassins and barbarians to skeletons and plants! Though as you’ll probably notice, the Horse was always going to make it into the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40171468/8654d361033c5c0e650cc5cd9b9c920e98caab2e.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40171468/1c0f2eeb614c89b9f66aa7bfe2de1a5df1130d37.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40171468/272a5155ca55de5570bab893d318e79cea51a2fa.jpg[/img]
For a while, we were even experimenting with the idea of each form having different evolutions. Some of these even made it into early versions of the game!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40171468/5e394b7c1fce68c9e4e9947fdf3f5014c96d9dd9.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40171468/67730affbfc4472e3c70698a56fd7b1f452d4c0e.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40171468/8680c2a30abaf05c6601de1cb6f895ce5da11b66.jpg[/img]
Making new locations and dungeons meant making a whole bunch of new tilesets and decorations which sometimes took a long time to do, so we had to get very strategic with what we decided to spend time on. Some of these concepts ended up inspiring what went into the ‘Frozen Hearth’ content.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40171468/70f15f313986eedfa3f6564e1f32049c42db0451.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40171468/481c011916e3fc62d934a2cb29c453f3c37009e9.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40171468/57b6c17484a2fc100d3ec1049cddef485fc01cf0.jpg[/img]
And let’s not ignore the incredibly ambitious early renditions of the world map with DOZENS of different locations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40171468/3a6f84b3ce3fe7979366ee78e77f7b20feb48ee5.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40171468/72fc396f8d71ee0f586a7fc76686d62f70a9276f.jpg[/img]
We wanted to make the enemies as cartoonishly icky as possible, and our incredible artists seemed to have a lot of fun coming up with all sorts of gruesome enemies. Admittedly, some of them look kinda cute (if you tilt your head and squint your eyes and imagine something cute).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40171468/1013acbe37cfcdf58908bf95c0cb848b892512ac.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40171468/d3e3b161c84d1748ffe028f5b974251e450002ff.png[/img]
The Calamity didn’t have a form for a long time, but we always knew it would be some kind of unimaginable eldritch horror. Not sure if any of us were prepared for what we saw when the time came to finally start penning the Calamity’s form. Just straight nightmare fuel.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40171468/d2ebb3378ad3aa46da02440e1af6263052778908.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40171468/0d405c216383c6b13b4c595a5a074736b8c967e5.jpg[/img]

And lastly, check out a few of the concepts we made for our two biggest updates to the game, “The Frozen Hearth” and “The Impossible Dungeon”. Did you know that Jimmy Luna was almost Jimmy Trash Panda?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40171468/f003b65266da38ab4673979964ed8b16371b4126.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40171468/3b2515903394579412f3885f02e0a56a4f77b28a.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40171468/6e772a98a2ec1e935577d97eb5ab9cbffdb9cf46.jpg[/img]
Thanks for all the love and support for Nobody Saves the World!
We know we’ve been pretty quiet for the last year or so while we work on our Next Big Thing™, surely we’d be able to share some news around it soon right? …right!?
Love,
The Drinkbox Team

notes.title: Impossible Dungeon Update
notes.content:
“IMPOSSIBLE DUNGEON” UPDATE NOTES:

- New Dungeon: A carnival themed "endless" dungeon which challenges players to quickly complete increasingly difficult floors under time pressure 
- Doing well in the dungeon rewards players with "tickets" which can be spent to build a large statue containing all of the game's forms
- New "Dino" form, with all new abilities and quests, unlocked by playing the Impossible Dungeon. The Dino form encourages players to swap between different damage types in order to gain damage boosting effects

ADDITIONAL BUG FIXES: 

- Gates at the start of the Frozen Hearth area could incorrectly close behind players
- Using Slime Slide twice quickly in succession could incorrectly make the starting puddle a damage zone
- Health leech was not being calculated correctly for some abilities when in a dungeon with the x9999 damage mod
- “0 mana required” modifier was not allowing some abilities to be performed when the player had 0 mana
- Some enemies would not be hit by turrets projectiles when projectiles were fired at certain angles
- Mechanic's leg animations could break when using arrow flurry
- Players could sometimes get stuck behind a rock in the Whackamelee! challenge room
- Summoning demons from turret deaths did not count towards the Necromancer's "Custom II: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle" quest
- Frozen Hearth level load screen was not properly centered
- Fixed issues with using some wireless / bluetooth controllers to play the game

notes.title: Impossible Dungeon Update OUT NOW!
notes.content:
Today is Nobody Saves the World’s first anniversary! To celebrate, we’re releasing a brand-new Impossible Dungeon update, out today for FREE! 

The update introduces a new carnival themed “endless” dungeon and a new Dinosaur form you can unlock by playing through the Impossible Dungeon.

[previewyoutube=DBAKGAFcfk4;full][/previewyoutube]
Step right up, and see if you’ve got what it takes to brave the challenges of Magic Jimmy’s Impossible Dungeon! Tucked away in a corner of the Alchemist’s Gorge area, players can test their skills on several floors of increasingly tough combat challenges while racing against the clock to try and get through each challenge as quickly as possible. This mode is perfect for Nobody Saves the World players who are looking for an endless combat challenge and a space to test new form combinations. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40171468/508a036e82b96a9526d2ee982cb34d9963e32237.jpg[/img]

Conquer the Impossible Dungeon, and be rewarded with the magical Dino Plushy that unlocks the new Dinosaur form! As with all other forms, the Dino comes with its own unique abilities and quests, and can be used throughout the entire game. Doing well in the dungeon will also reward players with tickets that can be used to build a commemorative statue of all the game’s forms.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40171468/11e5085c1e307f4a44ef27c76ce7d7fe3530df27.jpg[/img]
[i](Artwork by [url=https://twitter.com/_Mujizik/status/1559515403914825730]Matheus Meneguette[/url])[/i]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1432050/Nobody_Saves_the_World/ 

Thanks for all your support for Nobody Saves the World! This last year has been an amazing ride, and we couldn’t have done it without you. We hope you enjoy this new update!

[b]– The Drinkbox Team[/b]

notes.title: These five games will soon be leaving Xbox Game Pass
notes.content:
Five games are leaving Xbox Game Pass, and if you are interested in them, you'll want to download the titles as soon as possible.

Microsoft announced the following games are leaving the service within the next couple of weeks: The Anacrusis, Danganronpa: Trigger Happy Havoc Anniversary Edition, Nobody Saves the World, Pupperazzi, and Windjammers 2.

Game Preview title The Anacrusis is a four-player, cooperative first-person shooter set aboard a large starship stranded in space. In it, you team up with others to fight against alien hordes. In development at Stray Bombay Company, the title's AI Driver controls every aspect by spawning enemies, directing bosses, and placing every weapon, gadget, and health kit within the confines of the game. You will fight aliens using classic sci-fi weapons and earn new perks to change the way you play for infinite replayability.

notes.title: Drinkbox Studios 2022 year in review!

notes.title: Guacamelee devs swap Metroidvania for Diablo in Nobody Saves the World, out this month
notes.content:
The devs at Drinkbox Studios have built their reputation with colourful takes on the Metroidvania formula like Guacamelee and Severed, but they're taking a more Diablo-inspired path with the action-RPG Nobody Saves the World. Revealed back in April 2021, Nobody Saves the World has just gotten a proper release date for later this month.

Nobody Saves the World hits PC via Steam and PC Game Pass on January 18, 2022. (It also hits Xbox One, Xbox Series S and X, and console Game Pass on the same day.) If you want to pick it up with a standalone purchase rather than Game Pass, you can expect to pay $24.99 USD on your platform of choice. The game's online co-op features are supported for friends "within the same platform ecosystem", according to a press release.

The game casts you as a nobody - but one who can transform into over a dozen different forms, each of which has its own unique mechanics. You can create your own loadout by mixing and matching an array of abilities, as you delve into randomised dungeons in an effort to, as the title suggests, save the world.

notes.title: Multiplayer Reveal
notes.content:
Hi friends!

We’re excited to finally announce that our new Action RPG Nobody Saves the World will allow not just one, but two Nobodies to save the world. That’s right -- the game will arrive with two-player online co-op when it launches in early 2022! Twice the weird baby-lookin’ heroes! Twice the form-switching magic wands! Twice the Calamity-battling fun!!

[previewyoutube=-iEE1S5ApKI;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]How Co-op Works[/b]
Co-op works just like the main game, except you’re playing with a buddy. That means both of you can complete quests to level up, battle through unique dungeons, and mix-and-match abilities from different Forms. But since players can be seperate Forms, each with their own customizations, there’s a whole second layer of synergies that gets unlocked in multiplayer. 

[b]Multiplayer synergies[/b]
We’ve been testing co-op every day for the past 6 months-ish, so we can say from experience that there’s a lot of fun stuff you can do with two players:
🧟🐰Fill the screen with animal and zombie familiars
🐎🐎Knock enemies back-and-forth between you with the Horse’s powerful Kickback ability
🛡️🏹Use the Guard’s Shield to provide cover for the Ranger’s Arrow Flurry
📿🧜‍♀️Combine the Monk’s close-range fighting skills with the Mermaid’s aquatic mobility to dominate land and sea simultaneously!
This is only a small taste of what the game has to offer, and we can’t wait for you and your friends to dig in and experiment.

[b]Hop-in Multiplayer[/b]
It’s really easy to hop in-and-out of multiplayer too, since it uses your single-player saves. Want to make some progress in single-player, call in a friend for help with a dungeon, and then continue your game solo where you left off? You can!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40171468/162634aa9ee62c511d679f5fe3b5c57aa36e0ae2.jpg[/img]

We’re so pumped for you to explore this world, meet its characters, and defeat the Calamity with a friend when Nobody Saves the World launches in [b]early 2022.[/b]

notes.title: Drinkbox's Nobody Saves the World has all the lurid zip and levity of Guacamelee, with an RPG twist
notes.content:
There's a kind of innocence to some humour, an innocence it needs in order to work. You realise this when you think about Guacamelee, Drinkbox's breakout PS Vita hit - a game with these strange things called "memes" in it, a game named with a pun. I feel like we probably wouldn't enjoy a game with memes in it in 2021 - they're familiar now and sort of oddly important, and so you lose the innocence. But Drinkbox has kept the innocence elsewhere with Nobody Saves the World. It's another silly, but also seemingly very good, game that's built on humour first and clever evolution of genre just behind it, and another game named with a pun.

You play as someone called Nobody in Nobody Saves the World, which drops the wrestling metroidvania costume of Guacamelee (barring a few familiarly chicken-sized tunnels) for the fantastical cloak of a dungeon-crawling action RPG. It's not the genre I expected, after battering my way through Guacamelee, but it's a result of the studio wanting to keep "engaged and creative," as lead designer Ian Campbell put it, and the result is a game that feels the same: energetic and zippy and full of snap.

There are small twists on the genre. The first is that Nobody Saves the World is built around switching "forms" on the fly. Nobody is a blank and comically useless canvas of a character who nabs a special wand, the waving of which allows you to transform into one of what Campbell says is 17 or 18 forms available for the moment ("we're trying to do more but that's what we have right now"), each a little ridiculous and purposefully "non-standard". I took on my first dungeon as a rat, for instance, with some poison-y, gnawing attacks, and then unlocked a fairly run-of-the-mill ranger, followed by an odd, much less run-of-the-mill magician that summons rabbit familiars and jabs people with a fan of cards. There's a horse, and so on (I am not selling this as laugh-out-loud, I'm aware! But sometimes humour is simply levity, and Drinkbox has a magically light touch).
